newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady after day of consolidation.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady after day of consolidation.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed almost unchanged on Wednesday after a day of consolidation following Tuesday's sharp losses.

July Brent closed one cent up at $19.23 a barrel, having been lodged in a tight 25 cents range for the entire session. The contract shed 78 cents on Tuesday as investment funds liquidated their positions.
"It's just holding stable around unchanged, it's just taking a bit of a breather after yesterday and waiting for the APIs," said one broker shortly before the close.
Earlier June gas oil closed $1.00 a tonne higher at $173.00.
In the last few hours of trading, July Brent came off a low of $19.09, tracking NYMEX crude which bounced off support at $20.65 a barrel.
"It looked like there were stops at $20.65 on prompt WTI and the locals were good sellers, but it recovered from that level... and gasoline is holding up reasonably well too," said a broker.
Dealers said that the imminent release of weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) had stifled any bolder moves in the market.
Refinery capacity utilisation rates are expected to stay at or slightly below last week's high levels, showing oil product production is still running high, traders said.
This may pressure the gasoline market at a time when seasonal demand has failed to take its leading annual role, they said.

Together with foreign imports, high refinery runs are expected to ensure that the draw on gasoline stocks is only slight, despite expectations of a rise in gasoline consumption leading up to the three day Memorial Day weekend.
Estimates for crude inventories varied wildly with some traders expecting a draw of up to three million barrels and others predicting a build of the same amount.
Heating oil stocks were expected to show a build of around 1.6 million barrels.
